title: List of equipment of the Korean People's Army Ground Force

rows: Standard issue head gear for cold weather.
Standard issue head gear for non-cold weather.
United States Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Standard issued BDU, similar to the former camouflage uniforms of the ROK Army.
Unlicense copy. Some unit in KPA are issued, include the Special Force. Seen in 2022.
Seen in used by KPA troops on Russian Invasion of Ukraine.
Unlicensed copy of the FN Browning M1900. Can be fitted with a suppressor. Issued to high-ranking officers and spies.
Self-designed and produced; Modeled after the FN M1910, Makarov PM, and the Walther PPK; chambered in .32 ACP. Issued to high-ranking officers.
Unlicensed copy of the CZ 75 pistol. Replaced the Type 68 as the standard-issue pistol.
Issued to spies with suppressors attached.
Issued to spies with suppressors attached.
Canadian-made copies issued to spies and special forces commandos.
Both Soviet PPS submachine guns and Chinese Type 54s.
Resembles the PP-19-01 Vityaz and PP-19 Bizon but with an optical sight and a flash suppressor. Used by special forces.
Seen in use with North Korean troops in the Kursk region.
Resembles an AKS-74 but with a top-folding stock and has typically a helical magazine attached or in some cases a 30-round magazine. Preferred by mainly Special Operations Forces within the KPA

North Korean copy of the Russian AK-105 with a shortened 20-round magazine carrying 5.45×39mm ammunition. The furniture such as the pistol grip and the lightweight stock are made of plastic. Issued to armored crews.
North Korean copy of the AKM.
Unlicensed copy of the AK-74. It can use a 100 or 150-round helical magazine besides conventional 30-round box magazines.
Seen in use with North Korean troops in the Kursk region.
Bullpup Type weapon based on the Type 88-2 and ADS, Russian bullpup rifle chambered to fire the 5.45 mm round, fitted with a scope and a vertical handgrip. Issued to special force members

OICW-Type weapon based on the Type 88-2 chambered to fire the 5.45 mm round, as well as a 20 mm bullpup bolt-action over-barrel launcher with magazine containing around 5 rounds of programmable airburst grenades.
Limited use, issued to special force members.
Limited use, unlicensed locally made copies, issued to special force members at least since 1990s.
Limited use, unlicensed locally made copies, issued to special force members. Seen in use by North Korean Commandos in the Gangneung incident in 1996.
Unlicensed version of the PSL rifle, some sources say it's a Zastava M76 copy, chambered in 7.62x54mmR.
North Korean copy of the RPK machine gun, produced under license.
Indigenous design based on the ZB vz. 26 and the Kalashnikov PK machine gun design. Replaced by the Type 82 in service.
Indigenous electric-powered Gatling-type gun, chambered to fire 7.62×54mmR.
North Korean copy of the PKM machine gun. Replaced the Type 73 as the KPA standard general-purpose machine gun.
Standard issue. The Chinese Type 54 machine gun is also used by the KPA.
Chinese copies are also used by the KPA.
Underbarrel grenade launcher. Can be mounted on all Kalashnikov-type rifles.
Reported to have been used to illuminate two US Army Apache helicopters in 2003.
Based on the T-62, it incorporates technologies from the T-72 or T-90 tank.
Based on the T-62 and T-72, upgraded with a 125 mm main gun, improved fire control systems, infrared sensors, and laser rangefinders.
Similar to the PT-76, but uses the VTT-323 chassis.
6×6 and 8×8 versions based on the BTR-60 and BTR-80.
Non line of sight anti-tank guided missile carrier
6x6 vehicle equipped with non-ballistic missile system for armored targets and helicopters at long range (15-25 km) connected by trailing fiber-optic transmitting video back to vehicle.
Locally produced copy of the GAZ-51.
Civilian trucks converted for military use.
North Korean copy of the KAMAZ-58111, built in cooperation with KAMAZ.
Heavy civilian truck converted into a TEL.
Turret mounted mortar on a VTT-323 chassis.
D-30 mounted on a tracked chassis. Maximum range 15.3 kilometres (9.5 mi) or 21.9 kilometres (13.6 mi) with rocket-assisted projectiles.
A-19 mounted on a modified ATS-59 chassis. Maximum range 20.8 kilometres (12.9 mi).
D-1 mounted on a Type 63 chassis. Maximum range 12.4 kilometres (7.7 mi).
Juche 107th Year Type 155 mm Self-propelled Howitzer

155 mm SPH, first publicly displayed in a 2018 military parade. Range estimated to be over 30 kilometres (19 mi). Range of 40 kilometers. Striking range at over 60 kilometers as stated by North Korea. On June 25, extended-range artillery shells were fired during testing with range of 65 kilometers.
Locally produced Type 63 under license. Over 5,000 built for domestic and export markets.
Type 75 mounted on a Type 63 APC or VTT-323 chassis.
30-tube locally produced copy of the BM-21, mounted on a Ural-375D chassis.
North Korean copy of the BM-21 Grad.
40-tube locally produced copy of the BM-21, mounted on an Isuzu 6×6 chassis.
12-tube launcher mounted on an Isuzu 6×6 chassis.
Can fire unguided and guided rockets.
Maximum range of 240mm rocket stated at 100 for ballistic trajectory and 115 kilometers for glided.
North Korean copy of the OTR-21 Tochka.
North Korean copy of the 9K111 Fagot, it uses a laser guidance system.
8-tube launcher mounted on a M-2010 6×6 APC chassis.
Indigenous design, it resembles the Igla-1 with elements from the 9K38 Igla and 9K338 Igla-S.
Indigenous copy of the Igla-1, or the 9K38 Igla.
ZPU-4 gun mounted on a Chonma-ho chassis. Effective range 1.4 km (0.87 mi)
Twin 23 mm guns mounted on a modified ATS-59 chassis. Effective range 2.5 km (1.6 mi)
Twin 37 mm guns mounted guns possibly based on the M1939 mounted on a modified ATS-59 chassis.
Twin 57 mm guns mounted on a modified Type 63/YW531 chassis.
ZPU-1, ZPU-2, and ZPU-4 variants used. Produced locally.
